Let me analyze the submission against the rubric.

C1: Mission concept and rationale (40% weight, but levels 0-10 scaled presumably to max 40... Actually the criteria list max 40, weight 40, levels min 0 max 10. So mark out of 10, scaled to 40? I'll give mark within the level range (0-10) for each criterion. Hmm, but weights differ. The rubric lists "weight" 40/30/10/20 and max 40/30/10/20 but levels 0-10. I'll give the level mark out of 10 as that's what the level descriptors use. Actually to be safe, I'll give mark within the level range (which is defined 0-10). That's what "then a whole-number mark within that level's range" says.

C1: Mission concept is decent: coral reef monitoring satellite for Great Barrier Reef, users: marine/conservation scientists, rationale with citations. Requirements: sea surface temp, thermal stress, bathymetry, colour/tone detection. Lacks specific quantitative mission requirements (resolution, revisit, coverage, lifetime, orbit). No explicit statement of objectives as measurable requirements. Good narrative though with references. Adequate-to-Accomplished. I'd say Accomplished bottom: 7. Hmm. The Accomplished descriptor requires "clear and complete description of mission goals, objectives, and requirements". Requirements are not really quantified — no revisit time, spatial resolution targets (only mentions existing 100 m/pixel bathymetry as a benchmark), no data latency numbers (near-real-time), no mission lifetime. Users identified (marine and conservation scientists, monitoring stations). Literature references present (footnotes + links). I'd say Adequate high (6) or Accomplished low (7). I lean 6 or 7. Given the description is fairly strong but lacks quantitative requirements, I'll give 7 (Accomplished low) — actually "complete" is the issue. I'll go 6, Adequate, high.

Hmm, let me think. The rubric's C1 weight 40 but seems out of 10. Many such rubrics: mark out of 10 per criterion then weighted. I'll be consistent.

I think C1 deserves Adequate 6: good narrative and user identification, but requirements are not specified as requirements (no numbers, no explicit objectives list). Alternatively 7. I'll choose 6.

C2: Project plan — Gantt chart included with weeks and tasks, descriptions of each task, deadlines. No contingency provision (except week 10 for review/amendments, which is somewhat contingency). The plan relates to the mission (tasks like launch, orbit, ground control, comms, EOL). However, weeks listed Wk2–Wk10 starting 21/9 — dates seem odd (21/9 to 16/11 is ~8 weeks). Also no explicit contingency beyond "week 10 reserved for review". Information sources listed in "Useful Links". Reasonably good. No software rationale—STK is mentioned (allowed). C2: Adequate high or Accomplished low. The Accomplished requires provision for variations and contingencies and clear why plan developed this way in context of mission. There is an editing/finalisation week and mentions of iterative research. I'd give 7. Let me weigh: plan is present, detailed task descriptions, but no explicit contingency/risk, week numbering inconsistency, and dates: Wk2 21/9, Wk3 28/9, Wk4 5/10, ... Wk10 16/11 — that's 9 columns for Wk2-Wk10, fine. But 21/9 to 16/11 is 8 weeks; column dates weekly: 21/9,28/9,5/10,12/10,19/10,26/10,2/11,9/11,16/11 = 9 weeks. Fine. Actually week 10 is 16/11 and final report due 20/11 — consistent.

I'll give C2 = 7 (Accomplished low) since it has structure, task descriptions, links to mission, and info sources; contingency is only implicit. Hmm, "Acapable..." Actually I'd be comfortable with 6 (Adequate) given no explicit contingency plan and no risk/variation provision, and Gantt lacks milestones/resources. But there are deadlines in red. I'll go 6? Let me decide: the plan is functional and detailed, week 10 reserved for amendments/reflection which constitutes contingency-ish. I'll award 7.

Hmm—being a strict marker: C2 descriptor Accomplished requires "provision for project variations and contingencies" and "makes clear why the plan is developed this way in the context of the mission". The student does explain why background research is ongoing and why strategies are refined iteratively ("as I further explore launch and orbit"), and STK design/simulations run throughout. That's contextual justification. Contingency: week 10 for review/amendments. I'll give 7.

C3: Preliminary progress — technical content (10%). Progress: read literature, completed STK tutorials 1-4, Gantt complete. No actual technical results — no orbit calcs, no link budget, no STK simulation output. "Minor work completed ... results description insufficient" — Adequate? Deficient says "No actual or useful work completed." Completing STK tutorials and doing background research is some work but no technical results. I'd say Adequate low: 4. Actually there's essentially no technical content: no numbers computed, no design trade-offs quantitatively. Tutorials completed is learning, not design. I'd give 4 (Adequate) or 3 (Deficient high). Given "minor work completed" fits — some work done (research + tutorials) but no technical results. I'll give 4? Hmm, the descriptor "Minor work completed on the project. Results description or interpretation may be insufficient." Yes that fits: minor work (tutorials, background reading), no results. So Adequate 4, maybe 3. I'll go 4.

Actually the criterion is "Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date". There is essentially no technical content. But the mission concept writing is arguably progress. I'll give 4.

C4: Presentation (20%). Well structured with headings, readable prose, footnotes and a reference list (useful links) — but the in-text superscript references are URLs rather than author-date, and the reference list is just bare URLs, not properly formatted citations. Image 1: Gantt chart labelled with colour legend given in text; but the caption? It's "Image 1" with no figure caption/number in the text ("as seen above"). The Gantt has no title/label. Also section heading structure okay. Spelling/grammar good. References in text match references reasonably but reference list is bare links without titles (conversion artifact? The OCR gave bare URLs; possibly the student just pasted links). Formatting: hard to judge but reasonable. I'd give Adequate high 6 or Accomplished low 7. Given references are poorly formatted (bare URLs, repeated) and the figure lacks a caption, I'd give 6. Hmm, but overall the document reads very well and is well-written with clear headings. The main weakness is referencing style and unlabelled figure. I'll give 7? The Accomplished descriptor says "All aspects of formatting are consistent... References in text match reference list and are cited properly." Bare URLs aren't proper citations. So Adequate: 6.

Total: C1 6, C2 7, C3 4, C4 6. Since these are out of 10 and weights, total would be... The overall is qualitative.

Requirements:
R1: yes — mission concept, users, rationale.
R2: partial — plan touches launch and orbit tasks but no actual application of course material (no orbit/launch analysis), only plans to. "Relate the preliminary plan to the mission's space segment, applying relevant course material such as launch and orbits" — they mention reviewing launch vehicles, choosing orbit, COEs & AOEs. That's planning, not applying. Partial.
R3: yes — STK selected ("STK Design", "STK simulations", "completed STK tutorials 1,2,3,4"). STK is on the allowed list.
R4: yes — Gantt chart.
R5: yes — Useful Links; though mostly bare URLs; not labelled by content.
R6: partial/no — preliminary technical content minimal (no calculations). I'd say partial (background research + tutorials, no technical results).

Technical issues:
- 100 m/pixel bathymetry — GBR depth model from deepreef: actually the 30 m resolution model exists (Landsat-derived, 30 m for shallow reefs, 100 m for entire GBR). Fine.
- "Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic since the industrial revolution" — usual figure is ~30% increase in hydrogen ion concentration (i.e., 0.1 pH decrease). Wording is loose but commonly stated; slight technical imprecision — ocean acidification is a ~0.1 pH drop = 30% increase in acidity. Could note.
- Coral reef area 344,400 km² — GBR Marine Park area is ~344,400 km², correct (that's the Marine Park, not just reef).
- "2016 bleaching killed 30 percent of the reef's coral, 2017 another 20 percent" — commonly cited figures (2016: 29% loss of coral; 2017: 22% loss) but these are losses of coral cover in the northern region (2016) — figures are somewhat simplified; the 2016 event killed ~29% of shallow-water corals overall (ARC Centre). Acceptable.
- "near-real-time relay to monitoring stations" — no discussion of data latency/downlink architecture, ground station.
- No orbit or spatial resolution/revisit requirements specified; bathymetry detection of colour change requires high resolution (metres), conflicting with the 100 m/pixel reference which they cite as current limitation but don't set a target.
- No satellite bus/payload concept, no lifetime, cost, or Australian benefit explicitly in economic terms (benefit stated as environmental/scientific).
- Gantt chart: no explicit contingency; weeks lack milestones; "Wk 2" start missing week 1.
- Software: STK mentioned only in context; no justification/rationale for selecting STK.
- References: bare URLs, no titles/authors/access dates; footnotes duplicated in list.
- "30 percent more acidic" also no citation? It's footnote 1 to NOAA.
- "bathymetry (current satellites have only mapped GBR depths to a resolution of 100 meters per pixel)" — footnote 3 deepreef; the 100 m depth model is one product; the Allen Coral Atlas / Landsat gives 10-30 m; slight overstatement but sourced.

Also "Reef-monitoring satellites could also be used to report sea surface temperatures" — SST and thermal stress are already provided by NOAA Coral Reef Watch, which is in the useful links; the concept doesn't differentiate from existing capability (Coral Reef Watch already does SST/thermal stress). That's a gap in novelty/rationale—partially addressed by mentioning colour/tone change as new.
